verdict.rationale: Gmail's documented REST API covers the full loop an external agent would need: it can access mailboxes and threads, manage labels and filters for triage, create drafts and send them via drafts.send or messages.send, and receive push notifications, all authorized via OAuth scopes. However, the evidence shows no agent-native connection such as an MCP server, an official Claude/ChatGPT connector, llms.txt or an OpenAPI spec. Community reports also describe coarse scopes and a costly third-party security assessment for apps that need read access, which burdens a self-built agent. Missing for 10: an official agent connector or MCP endpoint, machine-readable API descriptions (llms.txt/OpenAPI returned 404), fine-grained scoping for agent access, and hands-on evidence of an external AI agent running read-triage-draft-send end to end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection

citations.quote: The Gmail API is a RESTful API that lets you access Gmail mailboxes and send mail.
The Gmail API lets you view and manage Gmail mailbox data like threads, messages, and labels.
You can send it from a draft, using the drafts.send method.
Email organization including filtering and sorting of messages
The Gmail API provides server push notifications that let you watch for changes to Gmail mailboxes.
